stage1.impression: A clean, evenly lit showroom corner, not a bar at night: the frame is exposed like daytime (median 99), the round table top and the shelf fronts are close to blown, and colour comes from everywhere at once (red and blue pendants, eight tinted globes in a row, striped record spines), so the red speaker is only one coloured object among many. The board-formed concrete wall and cabinet fronts are believable at 1:1 and the speaker's acrylic reads as thick, tinted and well made. But the evenly spaced row of lamps on lit shelves, the floating glowing EARF letters and the over-sharpened, grainy finish make it a catalogue page. A design magazine would not run it as a specific place. It reads as a generic product showroom.

blocking_9: Night exposure: frame lum_median 22-50 with pools of light and dark between them. It is now 99.3, with the floor at about 118-141 and no falloff.
No near-white surfaces outside the lamps: the table top region [290,560,570,640] is at lum_median 225 and the shelf front band [160,320,610,370] clips 1.6 %.
The Ember Tropos must be the clear hero: the brightest saturated object, with the light through its acrylic reading first. Today the pendants and the eight globes compete with it at equal weight.
The shop wall must read as a curated shop in a bar, not a lit display case: no glowing shelf-edge lines, lamps grouped rather than drilled in a row, and the price cards legible.
A photographic finish: no sharpening halos or coarse grain on the concrete and floor.
Signs of life and specificity in frame. The room's centrepiece (Mother EARF and its coloured shadow) is not visible, so nothing says this is Planet EARF and not any showroom.

defects.what: Overexposed for a night interior: lum_median 99.3, mean 112.8, only 19.7 % of pixels below 40.
The table top under the Dome downlight is near white (median 225, p95 238). It reads as a white disc, and the oak grain is lost.
The shelf fronts glow as bright lines (median 152, clip 1.6 %), like LED strips in a display case.
Eight Core lamps drilled in an even row at identical spacing: a catalogue line-up. No price cards are legible.
The EARF letters glow and float on the concrete, half hidden behind the white pendant. They read as signage.
A tall, bright vertical band on the left-hand return (median 163) draws the eye out of the frame at its edge.
The floor is flat and bright (y profile 143, 68, 91, 129, 137, 141, 142, 136), with no pool of light and no falloff toward the camera.
At 2x, sharpening halos at the cabinet joints and coarse luminance grain on the concrete and the fluted counter.
The tub chair, cut by the bottom edge, is a crushed black mass (crush 13 %) with no leather sheen.
Saturated red and blue pendant shades compete with the speaker for colour.

out_of_scope.request: Fewer tinted products on the shop wall (one tint, or smoked lamps only) so the speaker is the only saturated colour.
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the eight Core lamps in EARF's tints and the tinted pendants as products. This is the main thing that keeps the frame below a 9 against the 'one colour' bar. Ask the owner whether a shop shot may show one tint family.

out_of_scope.request: Lose the bright vertical return on the left [90,0,145,660] by changing its material or removing it.
out_of_scope.why: It is part of the room's design as proposed. Only its finish (sheen) or the camera may change; c8 helps.
